Connectome exploratory data analysis — v1

Scope: exact metadata for source files; full-row summaries of 256 randomly selected training sequences and 64 fixed development sequences; 512 post-warm-up rows per sequence for multivariate diagnostics. Confirmation and reserved validation rows remain untouched. This report contains descriptive analysis, not validated model improvements.

Measured findings

  • Analyzed all rows in 256 training sequences (5,120,000 rows) and all 64 fixed development sequences (1,280,000 rows). Confirmation and the other validation rows were not read for distribution analysis.
  • Feature nonfinite counts in analyzed rows: train 0; development 0. Arrow null counts: train 0; development 0. This is not a full-file integrity claim.
  • Development selects 118,431 rows, 9.30% of required prediction rows. Scored runs have median length 2.0 rows. Scoring-mask information is never an inference input.
  • Largest marginal feature shift: i1_v18, KS distance 0.3099. Sequence-held-out domain classifier AUC: logistic 0.7218, shallow boosting 0.8733. This indicates separability of these samples, not knowledge of the test distribution.
  • Sequence-held-out development mask classifier AUC: logistic 0.7906, shallow boosting 0.8085. A single split is exploratory and is not evidence that a hidden test mask follows the same mechanism.
  • t0 on scored development rows: zero fraction 16.84%; targets beyond +/-2 3.73%; largest 10% of rows account for 28.17% of metric weight. Weight-based effective sample size 67,462 ignores temporal dependence and is not an uncertainty estimate.
  • t1 on scored development rows: zero fraction 17.19%; targets beyond +/-2 3.33%; largest 10% of rows account for 28.30% of metric weight. Weight-based effective sample size 67,494 ignores temporal dependence and is not an uncertainty estimate.

Interpretation and next experiments

  • Prioritize a causal change/EMA feature baseline and a trainable GRU. Target autocorrelation and lagged-feature correlations describe dependence; neither is proof of an exploitable causal signal.
  • Audit extreme repeated values before adding sentinel indicators. Values below -4 are only a diagnostic threshold; the undocumented feature transforms do not establish that these values mean missing data.
  • Compare all-eligible and scored target distributions. Their difference describes selection, not an instruction to predict only on visible scored rows.
  • Use train/development shift diagnostics to motivate robustness checks. Do not assume the hidden test follows development or train a mask-specific predictor without independent evidence.
  • Investigate target discretization using per-sequence unique counts before proposing a classification head. No true target horizon, tick size, raw price, or raw spread is inferred by this report.
  • Fit all model preprocessing on training data. Sequence IDs only group rows; they are not chronological features. Never shuffle rows within a model sequence or use future rows in causal transforms.
  • Correlations, KS distances and PCA use sampled rows. Nearby rows remain dependent. No IID p-values or confidence claims are supplied. Group-held-out classifiers use one split and need repeated group splits before firm conclusions.
  • The fixed development set is now used for exploration. Keep confirmation out of training and tuning; full local validation is not independent of development.

Reproduction and outputs

python scripts/run_eda.py from the starter-pack root. Outputs are immutable: choose a new --output directory for another run. See summary.json, feature_shift.csv, per-dataset feature/sequence/lag tables, the correlation matrix, and environment.txt. No source data, trained challenge models, or raw sampled arrays are saved in this report folder.

EDA seed: 20261101. Source selection and hashes are in summary.json. No code or data is uploaded.
